headline: Agentic boom survives 2028 credit scare; productivity soars while office middle class hollows

events: Two frontier labs release agent systems that reliably run multi-day software, accounting and claims-processing workflows; enterprise adoption of AI in production jumps from 12% to 24%
Hyperscaler capex passes $750bn; US utilities file record interconnection requests and gas-turbine order books are full until 2031
Electricity prices in PJM, Texas and Ireland rise 15-25%, pushing G20 inflation back up to 3.8%; the Fed holds near 3.5% instead of cutting
Big Four accounting firms, Indian IT-services majors and US insurers announce hiring freezes; graduate entry-level postings drop by about a third
US-China agree a limited tariff truce covering chip equipment and rare earths; trade tensions plateau
Spring 'private-credit scare': a data-centre developer defaults on leveraged GPU-backed loans, Nasdaq falls 28% and credit spreads blow out for two quarters
The Fed cuts 125bp and the ECB 75bp; equities recover by year-end as AI firms post record margins
White-collar layoffs accelerate in call centres, back-office finance, paralegal work and translation; US unemployment hits 6.4%, Philippine and Indian BPO hubs shed about 2.5m jobs
US presidential campaign dominated by 'AI and jobs'; the winner promises a wage-insurance scheme and a compute levy
Inflation peaks at 4.4% G20 average as power, copper and transformer shortages feed through
Third capability jump: models with strong scientific-research ability compress drug-candidate and materials-discovery timelines; first AI-designed battery chemistry enters pilot production
US passes the Transition Security Act: 70% wage insurance for 2 years for displaced workers, funded partly by a 2% levy on large-firm AI revenue; deficit still widens to 7.5% of GDP
Global unemployment peaks at 6.9%; youth unemployment above 30% across North Africa and South Asia
Egypt, Pakistan and Kenya enter IMF-led restructurings as BPO and remittance income falls and dollar rates stay high
Humanoid and warehouse robotics scale in China; Beijing uses the productivity surge to offset its shrinking workforce and expands export of cheap automation kits
Measured US labour productivity growth hits 3.8%, the fastest since the 1960s; world growth reaches 4.2%
Mass protests in France, South Korea and Brazil against layoffs and soaring rents in AI-hub cities; a nationwide 'human work' strike in France lasts three weeks
Small modular reactor orders and record solar-plus-storage builds; AI-optimised grids cut curtailment, but coal plants in Asia and gas in the US run harder to meet data-centre load
Japan's 10-year yield breaches 2.5%, forcing the BoJ into renewed yield control; debt-service costs crowd budgets across advanced economies
A border war flares between Ethiopia and Eritrea, worsened by food-price shocks and unemployed militias
Over 60% of firms use AI in production; agentic software handles most first-line customer service, coding and routine legal drafting worldwide
Sri Lanka returns to default; G20 adopts a 'compute-for-development' facility, but it is small relative to lost services exports
Unemployment eases to 6.1% as care, construction, energy and in-person service jobs absorb workers, often at lower wages
Top 1% wealth share in the US reaches a record; the five largest AI firms account for 38% of S&P 500 value
EU finalises a digital dividend tax; populist parties lead polls in four of the six largest EU states

winners: Frontier AI labs, hyperscalers and their chip and power-equipment suppliers
Owners of land, grid connections and firm power near data-centre clusters
Skilled trades, nurses and care workers whose wages rise relative to office work
losers: Entry-level and mid-career white-collar workers in advanced economies
Services-export economies dependent on BPO and IT outsourcing (Philippines, India's tier-2 cities, Kenya)
Indebted frontier-market sovereigns facing high rates and weaker remittances
bullets: The world is richer and growing faster than in the 2010s, but the gains are concentrated among capital owners and a narrow class of AI-augmented professionals.
Office work has been hollowed out: graduate hiring is structurally lower and career ladders in law, finance and IT services have lost their bottom rungs.
Electricity, not chips, is the binding constraint; power prices and grid politics have become central to inflation and local elections.
Public debt keeps creeping up as wage insurance, retraining and higher interest costs offset AI-boosted tax receipts.
Trade friction stayed contained, but the Global South split between those with cheap power and data-centre deals and services exporters whose model collapsed.
Trust in institutions sank further as politics fixated on who owns the robots; populist and labour-protection movements are ascendant in Europe and Latin America.
Renewables grew fast, but surging data-centre demand kept fossil generation from falling, so emissions only plateaued and warming continued.
AI-accelerated science is starting to deliver concrete breakthroughs in drugs and materials, a source of cautious optimism for the 2030s.
wildcard: In 2028 a misconfigured autonomous trading-and-procurement agent swarm triggered a 40-minute freeze of European interbank payments, prompting the first binding international rules on agent liability.
image_description: In a converted Manila call-centre tower, former customer-service agents in hard hats learn to install heat pumps while delivery robots hum past a mural reading 'Humans Still Hired Here'.
